#MovingMinds

ETL

Process:

Extract: Data is extracted from various sources (databases, APIs, files)

Transform: Data is cleaned, transformed, and structured in a staging area before loading it into the target system, often involves filtering, aggregating, joining data, and enforcing data quality rules

Load: Transformed data is loaded into the target data warehouse or database

Benefits:

Improved data quality and consistency, optimized data warehouse performance as data is structured for analysis, better control over data transformations

Drawbacks:

Can be less flexible especially with evolving data requirements, may require significant upfront effort for data modelling and transformation design, potentially slower for large datasets or complex transformations

Example:

Used in financial reports (clean data before storage)

Colruyt extracts sales data from multiple stores, transforms it into a common format, and loads it into a central database for reporting

#MovingMinds

Example of ETL Pipeline

Data Source: CSV, APIs, Databases

Transformation: Remove Duplicates, fix formats, …

Target: Data warehouse

#MovingMinds

ELT

Process:

Extract: Data is extracted from various sources.

Load: Raw data is loaded directly into the target data lake or cloud data warehouse.

Transform: Data is transformed within the target system using its processing capabilities or dedicated transformation tools, leverages the scalability and processing power of modern data platforms.

Benefits:

Increased flexibility and agility to adapt to changing data needs, faster data loading as transformations are done later, scalability to handle massive datasets and complex transformations

Drawbacks:

Requires robust data governance and management to ensure data quality within the data lake, may require more complex data discovery and transformation tools, potential for higher storage costs as raw data is stored.

Example:

Used in data lakes (store raw data and transform if needed)

Evolution of ETL – From Batch to Real-Time

Traditional ETL

Batch processing with daily data updates

For example: banks processing transactions overnight

Modern ETL

Real-time data streaming

For example (fraud detection systems that process transactions instantly)

Future ETL

Cloud-based ETL and serverless computing are changing how we handle large-scale data -> eliminates infrastructure management

AI-powered ETL can detect anomalies and optimize transformations

Example: Netflix uses real-time ETL to recommend shows based on what you are watching.

Extract – Getting data from Different Sources

Types of Data Sources:

Relational Databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL)

NoSQL Databases (MongoDB)

APIs

Cloud Storage (AWS S3, GCS)

CSV, JSON, XML files

Example: A weather analytics company pulls data from IoT sensors, public APIs and weather satellites to make forecasts

#MovingMinds

Transform – Cleaning and Processing Data

Basic Transformations

Cleaning up missing or wrong values

Removing duplicates

Converting values (text to date, etc.)

Creating keys

Advanced Transformations

    • Calculating derived values
    • Filtering values / rows
    • Join or merge from two or more different sources
    • Splitting columns
    • Data validation
    • Summing and grouping
    • Aggregating
    • Integrating
    • NLP processing (text cleaning)
    • Anonymization & masking (scrambling)

Types of Transformations

  1. Structural transformations
  2. Semantic transformations
  3. Enrichment transformations
  4. Operational transformations

Structural Transformations

Changes the shape or schema of the data

Examples:

  • Column renaming
  • pivotting
  • normalization
  • Data type casting
  • Flattening nested JSON

Changes in structure, NOT meaning!

{ "order_id": 1, "customer": { "id": 101, "name": "Alice" } }

 |order_id|customer_id|customer_name|    

Challenges:

  • Schema mismatches
  • Nested data complexity
  • Performance cost of reshaping large datasets
  • Schema evolution impact

Semantic Transformations

Changes the meaning or interpretation of data

Examples:

  • Currency conversion (EUR -> USD)
  • Apply business rules, like calculating the revenue
  • Unit conversion (mile -> km)
  • Mapping category values ("M" -> "Male")
  • > Introduction to business logic
  • > Semantic transformations should be centralized, documented, version-controlled and testable

Challenges/risks:

  • Hardcoding business rules
  • Hidden assumptions
  • Rule changes over time
  • Inconsistent rule implementation across systems

Enrichment Transformations

Adds information from other sources

Examples:

  • Joining internal datasets
  • Joining external APIs
  • Geolocation enrichment
  • Feature engineering for Machine Learning

-> Enrichment increases analytical value, complexity and processing cost

Operational Transformations

Transforms data for system requirements, not business meaning

Examples:

  • Hashing IDs
  • Partitioning by date
  • Generate surrogate keys
  • Index optimization

-> Improvement of performance, scalability and storage optimization

Stateless versus Stateful Processing

Stateless -> Each record can be processed independently without remembering previous records.

Example:

  • Convert temperature
  • Clean a string
  • Hash a password
  • memory needed

Stateful -> The output depends on previous events.

Example:

  • Averages of sales
  • Fraud detection based on user history
  • Window-based aggregation
  • Memory needed

How is this related to batch and real-time processing?

Windowing

In streaming or real-time processing, data is infinite

You cannot compute the total sales ever because the streaming never ends

Tumbling Windows

Fixed-size non-overlapping windows

Every 5 minutesEvery hour

Sliding Windows

Overlapping windows

Last 10 minutes, updated every minute

Session Windows

Grouped by inactivity

A user browsing a website, session ends after 30 minutes of inactivity

Example: Sales Data Transformation

  • Raw Data: Sales data from multiple regions in different formats (e.g., CSV, Excel).
  • Transformation Process:
    • Cleaning: Removing duplicates and correcting errors.
    • Standardizing: Converting all data to a common format.
    • Aggregating: Summarizing sales data by region and time period.
  • Transformed Data: A unified dataset that provides clear insights into sales performance across regions.

Load – Storing Data Efficiently

Common Destinations for ETL Pipelines:

Data Warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery) -> Optimized for analytics

Data Lakes (AWS S3, Azure Data Lake) -> Stores raw data for later processing

Operational Databases (PostgreSQL) -> For application usage

Example: Spotify loads transformed used data into a data warehouse to generate personalized playlists.

#MovingMinds

Data Layers Overview

Modern data platforms use a layered approach

Organize data into progressive refinement layers:

    • Bronze = raw
    • Silver = cleaned & structured
    • Gold = curated & business-ready

Ensures traceability, quality, and usability

The Bronze, Silver and Gold Layers

  • Bronze (Raw Layer)
        • Stores raw ingested data (CSV, JSON, logs, IoT streams).
        • Minimal processing — just ingestion and basic validation.
        • Purpose: Preserve original data for replay/debugging.
  • Silver (Cleansed / Enriched Layer)
        • Data is cleaned, deduplicated, standardized.
        • Joins across sources, handles missing values, applies business rules.
        • Purpose: Create a single source of truth with consistent data.
  • Gold (Business / Analytics Layer)
        • Aggregated, curated data ready for BI, dashboards, ML models.
        • Optimized for specific use cases (sales reports, fraud detection, churn prediction).
        • Purpose: Enable decision-making and advanced analytics.

#MovingMinds

Importance of these layers

PROVIDES PROGRESSIVE REFINEMENT OF DATA (RAW →TRUSTED ACTIONABLE).→

IMPROVES DATA GOVERNANCE (LINEAGE CLEAR AT EACH LAYER).

ENABLES SELF-SERVICE ANALYTICS: DIFFERENT TEAMS CONSUME DATA AT THE RIGHT LEVEL.

SUPPORTS SCALABILITY IN MODERN ARCHITECTURES (LAKEHOUSES, STREAMING ETL).

  • Example:​
      • Bronze: IoT sensor data ingested in JSON format.​
      • Silver: Cleaned + joined with weather API.​
      • Gold: Aggregated for predictive maintenance dashboard.

Where does ETL fit?

Data flow in Modern Company:

Raw data ingestion

Processing & transformation (ETL, ELT)

Storage & analytics (Data warehouse, Data lake, BI tools)

Example: Uber’s architecture ingests real-time ride data, transforms it into trip summaries and loads it into dashboards used by drivers and managers

#MovingMinds

The Role of Metadata & Data Lineage in ETL

Metadata = data that provides information about other data

Metadata = key to trust in data

Data Lineage = Understanding where data comes from and how it is transformed

Governance and Auditing -> essential for industries like finance and healthcare

Example: A bank needs data lineage to track loan approval data – where it came from, how it was modified and who accessed it.

Intermezzo: DevOps

  • set of practices that combines software development (Dev) and IT operations (Ops).
  • shorten the development lifecycle and deliver high-quality software continuously.
  • Key Principles:
    • Collaboration: Enhanced communication between development and operations teams.
    • Automation: Automating repetitive tasks to increase efficiency.
    • Continuous Improvement: Regularly refining processes and tools.

#MovingMinds

Intermezzo: CI/CD

  • Continuous Integration (CI):
    • The practice of frequently integrating code changes into a shared repository.
    • detect and address integration issues early.
    • Key Practices:
      • Automated Testing: Running tests automatically to ensure code quality.
      • Frequent Commits: Regularly merging code changes to avoid conflicts.
  • Continuous Deployment (CD):
    • The practice of automatically deploying code changes to production.
    • deliver new features and fixes quickly and reliably.
    • Key Practices:
      • Automated Deployment: Using scripts and tools to deploy code without manual intervention.
      • Monitoring: Continuously monitoring the system to ensure stability.

#MovingMinds

ETL Automation & DevOps – Making Pipelines Smarter

CI/CD for ETL pipelines -> Version-controlled ETL scripts

DataOps -> Applying DevOps principles to ETL

Automated Testing for ETL -> Validating data quality before loading

Example: Spotify runs end-to-end ETL tests to verify playlist generation logic before updates go live.

#MovingMinds

ETLT

Hybrid approach where data is transformed both before and after loading.

Process:

    • Extract raw data from sources.
    • Transform lightly (data validation, basic cleaning).
    • Load into data lake/warehouse.
    • Transform again inside the target system for advanced analytics.

Why ETLT?

    • Balances data quality (early checks) with scalability (in-database transformations).
    • Reduces pipeline breakage by catching errors early.

Use Case:

    • Healthcare: Validate & mask sensitive data before storage, then perform heavy transformations (aggregation, ML prep) inside the data warehouse.

Tools: dbt, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks.

DataOps

Inspired by DevOps practices

Improve collaboration, automation, and monitoring in data engineering

Key principles:

    • Automation of pipelines (CI/CD for data)
    • Testing & validation of data quality
    • Monitoring for failures and anomalies
    • Collaboration across teams (data engineers, analysts, business)

Result: faster, more reliable, reproducible data delivery

#MovingMinds

Reverse ETL

Traditional ETL/ELT: data flows into warehouse

Reverse ETL: send data back out from warehouse into operational tools

    • Examples: CRM (Salesforce), marketing platforms, support tools

Enables operational analytics:

    • Sales team gets customer insights directly in Salesforce
    • Marketing can use ML-driven customer segments for campaigns

Bridges the gap between analytics & operations

#MovingMinds

Comparing ETL, ELT, ETLT and Reverse ETL

Approach

Process Flow

Strengths

Challenges

Example Use Case

ETL

Data transformed before loading

Ensures high data quality before storage; optimized for BI & reporting

Less flexible; slower for big/complex datasets

Financial reporting: Clean & aggregate transactions before warehouse load

ELT

Raw data loaded, transformed inside target system

Scales well; faster load; flexible for diverse data

Requires strong governance; higher storage costs

Cloud warehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake) transforms raw clickstream data

ETLT

Light transform before load + advanced transform after

Balances quality checks with scalability; early error detection

More complex pipeline to manage

Healthcare: Validate PHI before storage, then aggregate in warehouse

Reverse ETL

Push transformed data from warehouse back into apps

Operationalizes insights; enables real-time business actions

Harder to maintain sync; risk of stale data

Push churn-risk scores into Salesforce or CLV into HubSpot

#MovingMinds

Key Message

ETLT, DataOps, Reverse ETL = different approaches to the same challenge

Making data accessible, clean, and useful

They differ in where transformations happen, how pipelines are managed, and who consumes the data

Core data engineering concepts remain the same: ingestion, transformation, quality, delivery

Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD)

Used in data warehouses

The problem:

  • Customer attributes change over time.But analytics often requires historical correctness.

Example:

Customer moves from Belgium to France.

If we overwrite country:Historical sales appear French — incorrect.

SCD type 1 – overwrite

  • history preserved
  • Simple and fast

SCD type 2 – Preserve history

  • Add start-, end date and active flag
  • Each change creates a new row

ETL Challenges

  1. Handling Large Datasets

Can be fixed by using parallel processing

  1. Data Quality Issues

Can be fixed by automated validation and deduplication

  1. Performance Optimization
  2. Data Governance & Compliance

Can be fixed by encryption, access control or anonymization of sensitive data

A poorly designed ETL pipeline can lead to slow dashboards, incorrect reports, and compliance risks.

Common Pitfalls

Hardcoding business rules

  • Schema validation
  • logging

Duplicate transformations

Mixing ingestion with busingess logic

Over-aggregation too early

Can result in the "Silent Failure" Problem

#MovingMinds

The "Silent Failure" Problem

Worst case:

 Pipeline runs

 No error

 Wrong results

How to avoid this:

  • Validation checks
  • Reconciliation metrics

Idempotency

A process is idempotent if:

Running it multiple times produces the same result.

Example of non-idempotent pipeline:

Every run appends data again.

Result -> duplicates

Importance of idempotency

In practice:

  • Jobs fail
  • Jobs retry
  • Networks fail
  • Workers crash

If your data pipeline is not idempotent:

Retries will cause corrupt data

Why is Data Transformation important?

1. Enhances Data Quality

    • Removes inconsistencies: Cleanses data by correcting errors and inconsistencies.
    • Standardizes formats: Ensures uniformity in data representation.
    • Aggregation: summarizing large datasets, like monthly sales instead of daily sales.

2. Improves Data Usability

    • Facilitates analysis: Converts raw data into a usable format for analysis.
    • Enables integration: Allows data from different sources to be combined seamlessly.

3. Supports Decision Making

    • Provides accurate insights: Transformed data leads to more reliable insights.
    • Enhances reporting: Improves the quality and clarity of reports.

4. Security & Compliance

    • Masking personally identifiable information like emails or credit card numbers for GDPR compliance

Case Study- How Amazon Transforms Billions of Records

Scenario:

Amazon ingests & transforms massive e-commerce data for personalization

  • Extract: Logs from website, transactions, reviews
  • Transform: Aggregation, fraud detection, sentiment analysis
  • Load: Redshift data warehouse for analytics

Summary & Key Takeaways

  • ETL is essential for transforming raw data into actionable insights
  • ETL vs ELT depends on storage, processing needs and scalability
  • Performance optimization, automation and cloud-based solutions improve ETL efficiency

Building robust ETL pipelines ensures data is always ready for analytics, decision-making and AI applications
